title: Intermittent p95 regression harness and cost synthesis across A10/L4/A100/H100
creator: Priya Shah
description: Run a focused benchmarking and load testing campaign to isolate intermittent p95 latency regressions observed under bursty request patterns. The goal is to produce a reproducible harness that exposes transient p95 spikes across GPU families (A10, L4, A100, H100), quantify tokens/sec under steady vs. burst regimes, and synthesize a cost-per-token model that accounts for queuing overhead and tail amplification. This ticket covers harness design, experiment runs, initial triage, and a short remediation proposal (software or config-level).
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproducible harness that can run stable and burst workloads on A10/L4/A100/H100 with templated configs.
- p95 regression detector implemented that raises alerts when p95 degrades by >20% relative to baseline after smoothing.
- Consolidated cost-per-token report including nominal, burst, and tail-adjusted metrics for each GPU and instance pricing tier (on-demand vs reserved).
- Playbook entry with triage steps and at least two candidate mitigations (e.g., batch caps, KV cache warmup policy, routing change).
test_plan:
1) Implement replay driver that can emit steady (100 qps) and bursty (800 qps for 30s every 5 minutes) traffic with real request length distribution sampled from production.
2) Run three replicates on each GPU type: cold-start (after node restart), warm (after 10 minutes of steady traffic), and stressed (sustained burst for 1 hour).
3) Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length, GPU utilization, and model process stall events.
4) Apply statistical smoothing (rolling median 1m) and run regression detector (CUSUM + thresholding) to flag transient shifts.
5) Calculate cost-per-token as: (instance-hour-cost * runtime_seconds) / tokens_generated, and a tail-adjusted cost accounting for wasted compute during latency spikes.
results_summary: Preliminary runs show a consistent pattern: L4 and A100 deliver best steady tokens/sec for short-context workloads; H100 leads for long-context due to memory bandwidth. Intermittent p95 spikes during bursts correlate with kernel scheduling stalls on A10 and L4 in our runtime (observed 2-3x p95 increase for 30-90s windows). Token-economics: nominal cost-per-token (steady) ranges: A10 $0.00034, L4 $0.00028, A100 $0.00022, H100 $0.00019 (on-demand pricing assumptions). Tail-adjusted cost (including 95th percentile amplification) increases A10 and L4 costs by ~45% and A100/H100 by ~18%. Detailed CSVs and dashboards linked in artifacts.
observations:
- Burst-induced p95 spikes typically start ~5-12s after burst onset and often persist beyond the burst window due to KV cache coldness and re-privileging of kernels.
- CUSUM-based detector catches sustained regressions but misses short, high-amplitude spikes; hybrid rule added (absolute p95 > baseline*1.4 for >15s) improves recall.
- Batching caps (per-request batch_limit=8) reduced stall amplification on A10 by 30% at the cost of ~6% throughput loss.
- Scheduling knobs (prefer low-latency kernel variants) reduced tail on H100 but increased GPU utilization by ~4%.

next_steps:
1) Run expanded matrix with instance reservation pricing models (1yr reserved vs on-demand vs spot) to refine cost-per-token.
2) Add KV cache warmup policy to replay driver and measure improvements.
3) Postmortem candidate: implement adaptive batch cap that scales down during burst onset and re-expands after 30s without p95 spikes.
4) Schedule review with runtime team and PM for prioritization and release slot in runtime-1.20.
